skill.name: env-doctor-free
skill.description: Diagnose local startup failures across Node, Python, Go, and Docker projects by checking runtimes, dependencies, ports, environment keys, permissions, and services.
skill.summary: Find and prioritize local environment problems before changing application code.
skill.author: justhandledlabs

security_audit.summary: All 108 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, environment key names, and adversarial safety fixtures. The skill limits diagnostics to local resources, suppresses environment values, and requires approval before stopping processes. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious command flow was found.

content.value_statement: Local applications often fail because runtimes, dependencies, ports, variables, permissions, or services are misconfigured. Env Doctor checks these conditions and returns prioritized, platform-specific fixes without exposing environment values.
actual_capabilities: Detect Node, Python, Go, and Docker projects from standard project files.
Check installed runtime and package manager versions using platform-appropriate commands.
Identify missing dependencies, virtual environments, writable directories, and executable script permissions.
Inspect common local development ports and report the owning process before any stop action.
Compare environment file key names and empty states without displaying or retaining values.
Identify likely Postgres, Redis, and MySQL service dependencies from project configuration.
limitations: Diagnoses local environment conditions, not defects inside application logic.
Checks environment variable presence and emptiness, but cannot verify whether a supplied value is correct.
Requires user approval before process termination and does not perform force stops automatically.
Installer, service start, and dependency repair commands may change files or local state.

use_cases.title: Restore a Local Project
use_cases.description: Find missing runtimes, dependencies, variables, or services that prevent an application from starting.

use_cases.title: Resolve Shared Port Conflicts
use_cases.description: Identify which local process owns a development port before choosing a targeted, approved remediation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Onboarding Checks
use_cases.description: Run a consistent environment checklist for new contributors across Node, Python, Go, and Docker projects.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Startup Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why this project does not start. Detect the project type, check required runtimes and dependencies, then provide a prioritized checklist.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a guided first diagnosis.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Port Conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether port {port} is occupied on {operating_system}. Identify its owner, explain the evidence, and ask before suggesting any stop action.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs to resolve an occupied local port.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Environment Keys
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare .env.example with .env for this {framework} project. Report only missing, empty, or present key names, and never expose values.
prompt_templates.scenario: A service fails because required configuration may be absent.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Polyglot Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository's Node, Python, Go, and Docker requirements. Correlate runtime versions, dependencies, ports, permissions, environment keys, and service status. Rank root causes by impact and include only commands for {operating_system}.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a complete cross-stack environment review.

output_examples.input: A Node project has no node_modules directory and npm is available.
output: Evidence: package.json exists, npm is available, and node_modules is absent.
Fix: Install dependencies with the package manager selected by the lockfile.
Likely start command: Use the start or development script declared in package.json.

output_examples.input: Port 3000 is owned by an unrelated video conference process on Windows.
output: High: Port 3000 is already in use by an unrelated process.
Evidence: The listener owner and process identifier do not establish project ownership.
Fix: Keep the process running unless the user approves a targeted stop or selects another application port.

output_examples.input: A Django project requires DATABASE_URL, but the key is absent from the local environment file.
output: Evidence: The example file requires the key, and the local file does not contain it.
Fix: Add a valid value locally without sharing it in the diagnostic output.

best_practices: Run diagnosis from the project root so file markers and dependency checks use the correct scope.
Review every proposed installer, service start, or file mutation before execution.
Keep environment values private; share only key names and present, empty, or missing states.
anti_patterns: Do not display complete environment files or include variable values in logs and findings.
Do not terminate a process until its ownership is confirmed and the user approves the exact action.
Do not mix Windows and POSIX commands in one copy-ready instruction block.

faq.question: Which project types are supported?
faq.answer: The skill detects Node, Python, Go, and Docker projects from their standard files.

faq.question: Does it display environment variable values?
faq.answer: No. It reports only key names and whether each key is present, empty, or missing.

faq.question: Can it stop a process using a required port?
faq.answer: It identifies the owner first. Any targeted stop requires explicit user approval, and force stopping requires separate approval.

faq.question: Can the diagnosis modify project files?
faq.answer: Most checks are read-only. Dependency installation or Go module repair may change files and should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Which local services can it identify?
faq.answer: It detects likely Postgres, Redis, and MySQL dependencies, then recommends non-destructive status checks.

faq.question: What happens when the environment looks healthy?
faq.answer: The result states that no environment issue was found and recommends the next application-level debugging step.
